snippets.output: The terms “flu test” and “influenza test” are often used interchangeably.
The terms “flu test” and “influenza test” can refer to different types of diagnostic tests for influenza virus infection.
A flu test typically refers to a rapid diagnostic test (RDT) that detects the presence of influenza virus antigens in respiratory specimens.

Respiratory specimens for a flu test for influenza virus infection can include nasal swabs or throat swabs. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) for influenza are usually rapid, point-of-care tests that provide results within 15–30 minutes.
An influenza test can refer to a more comprehensive diagnostic approach.

An influenza test can include various tests, including rapid antigen detection tests (RADTs), molecular tests such as reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), viral culture, and serological tests that detect antibodies against the influenza virus.
Influenza tests can be used to diagnose influenza virus infection, monitor the spread of the virus, and guide treatment decisions.
A flu test typically refers to a rapid diagnostic test for influenza virus infection.
An influenza test can refer to a broader range of diagnostic approaches for influenza virus infection.
